title: Sending email with Nodemailer
idea: Nodemailer sends email from Node. You create a transporter for one SMTP server, then call `sendMail` with a message object.
points: SMTP is the protocol programs use to hand an email to a mail server.
A transporter stores the host, port and login for one SMTP server.
`sendMail` takes `from`, `to`, `subject`, `text` and `html`, and returns a promise.
With `jsonTransport: true`, nothing is sent: the result holds the message as JSON.

hero.title: One email, from your code to an inbox

steps.caption: The transporter connects to `MAIL_HOST` on `MAIL_PORT` and logs in with `MAIL_USER` and `MAIL_PASS`.
It sends the message over that connection.
The server accepts the message and replies. Only now does the `await` in your code finish.
Delivery to the inbox happens after that. Your code never sees it.
With `jsonTransport: true` there is no server. The transporter returns the message as JSON and sends nothing.

code.title: src/utils/mail.js
code.caption: The project's `sendEmail`. It needs a real SMTP server, so it does not run here; the next snippet does.

walk.text: Mailgen builds the HTML and plain-text bodies. This setup came with the email templates.
Callers pass the recipient, the subject and a Mailgen content object.
The transporter reads the four `MAIL_*` values. Environment values are strings, so convert the port.
Send both bodies. Plain text serves clients that do not show HTML.
`await` resolves once the server accepts the message. A failure rejects and reaches the caller.

code.title: Send without a server
code.caption: The same message, sent through `jsonTransport`. Nothing leaves your machine, and you can inspect what would have been sent.

walk.text: A content object like the ones the previous lesson builds.
`jsonTransport` builds the message but sends nothing.
`info.message` is a JSON string. Parse it to inspect the message.
Check both addresses, the subject, and that both bodies carry the link.

pitfalls: Use `secure: true` on port 465. Elsewhere TLS happens only if the server offers STARTTLS.
Keep `MAIL_USER` and `MAIL_PASS` in `.env`. Never commit them or log the transporter.
Do not catch and hide errors in `sendEmail`: callers must learn when mail fails.

quiz.why: `jsonTransport` returns the message as a JSON string in `info.message`. Parse it to read fields such as `subject`.

takeaway: `sendMail` resolves when the server accepts the message, not when it is delivered.

starters: Which SMTP server should I use while developing?
Should `sendEmail` wait for the server before replying to the user?
